description: Frozen authored trigger specs for the en-es semantic-veto heuristic-group research packet.

cases.sentence: I missed your call during the meeting.
The call lasted only five minutes.
The referee made a close call near the goal.
They call the dog Luna because of her white fur.
They decided to call off the outdoor concert.

call.gloss_text: an act of contacting someone by telephone
call.review_notes: Very common noun/verb source with decision, naming, and phrasal uses.

shadows.gloss_text: a decision or judgment made by an official
to give a name to someone or something

cases.sentence: He wrote a check for the deposit.
The check cleared before Friday.
Please check the form before sending it.
The airport added a security check at the gate.
They need to check in before noon.

check.gloss_text: a written order directing a bank to pay money
check.review_notes: Outcome-informed sentinel; not used to validate the primary heuristic.

shadows.gloss_text: to examine something for correctness or safety
an examination or safety control

cases.sentence: The crisis forced the school to close.
During the crisis, volunteers delivered food.
Crisis Core was listed as the game title.

crisis.gloss_text: a time of intense difficulty, danger, or instability
crisis.review_notes: Low-polysemy cognate control; title mentions are the main negative shape.

cases.sentence: The hikers crossed a deep valley.
The deep water looked almost black.
His deep voice filled the room.
She fell into deep concentration.
Deep down, he knew the answer.

deep.gloss_text: extending far down, inward, or below the surface
deep.review_notes: Many adjective/adverb senses, but several Spanish targets overlap with profundo.

shadows.gloss_text: having a low pitch
strong, serious, or emotionally intense

cases.sentence: She wore a green jacket to school.
The green paint dried overnight.
The green intern needed extra training.
The mayor announced a green policy for buses.
The driver waited for the green light.

green.gloss_text: having the color of grass or leaves
green.review_notes: Color, environmental, inexperienced, and golf senses create a clean mid-rank test.

shadows.gloss_text: new and lacking experience
related to environmental politics or sustainability
the closely cut area around a golf hole

cases.sentence: He borrowed a hammer from the garage.
The hammer slipped off the nail.
Workers hammer the metal into shape.
The painting went under the hammer at noon.
She tried to hammer home the main point.

hammer.gloss_text: a hand tool with a heavy head used for hitting nails
hammer.review_notes: Tool target competes with verb and auction/sports extensions.

shadows.gloss_text: to hit something repeatedly with force
a gavel or mallet used to close an auction or meeting

cases.sentence: Thanks for your help with the boxes.
The instructions offer help for new users.
The farm hired help for the harvest season.
The help cleaned the rooms before noon.
I cannot help laughing at that scene.

help.gloss_text: assistance or support given to someone
help.review_notes: Mostly assistance, but staff and fixed expressions create realistic non-active cases.

shadows.gloss_text: people hired to do domestic or farm work

cases.sentence: The shelf is too low for the vase.
The store offered a low price.
The stock hit a new low after the report.
The cattle low softly near the barn.
Low and behold was written as a joke.

low.gloss_text: not high in position, amount, level, or degree
low.review_notes: Small tail word with many adjective/adverb/noun/verb uses.

shadows.gloss_text: the lowest point or level reached
to make the deep sound of cattle

cases.sentence: The old man waited by the bus stop.
A tall man entered the quiet room.
Volunteers man the phones during the pledge drive.
Two guards man the front gate after dark.
Man, that was a close call at the end.

man.review_notes: Common core word with noun and verb senses; useful overload probe.

shadows.gloss_text: to provide people to operate equipment, a booth, or a station
generic human or mankind sense rather than specifically male adult

cases.sentence: He saved money for the trip.
They raised money for the clinic.
Money talks in that old proverb.

money.gloss_text: coins, bills, or funds used for payment
money.review_notes: Low-polysemy control with phrase risk rather than true shadow competition.

cases.sentence: She often rides her bike to work.
We often meet after class.
Little and often is his training motto.

often.review_notes: Low-polysemy adverb control; negative case is a fixed expression.

cases.sentence: Your order shipped this morning.
The waiter took our order quickly.
The judge issued a strict order.
Sort the names in alphabetical order.
She left early in order to catch the train.

order.gloss_text: a request to buy goods or food
order.review_notes: Outcome-informed sentinel with commerce, command, and sequence senses.

shadows.gloss_text: an authoritative command or legal instruction
the arrangement of things in a sequence

cases.sentence: Each participant signed the consent form.
The participant asked a question after class.
The database field participant id was blank.

participant.gloss_text: a person who takes part in an activity
participant.review_notes: Low-polysemy person noun; code/field mentions are the main no-winner shape.

cases.sentence: We need a particular tool for this repair.
She had no particular reason to leave.
He is particular about the spacing in reports.
The lawyer checked every particular of the claim.
That problem matters in particular today.

particular.review_notes: Specific-sense target competes with fussy and detail-noun senses.

shadows.gloss_text: very exacting or fussy about details
individual facts or details of a case

cases.sentence: Only ten percent of the class passed.
The rate rose by three percent last month.
The percent sign appeared in every spreadsheet cell.

percent.review_notes: Low-polysemy numeric control; only mention/format phrases act as negatives.

cases.sentence: They plant tomatoes behind the house.
We plant trees along the road each spring.
The plant needs sunlight every morning.
The power plant hired new engineers.
The spy tried to plant evidence in the room.

plant.gloss_text: to put seeds or plants in the ground so they grow
plant.review_notes: Outcome-informed sentinel; active is verb to avoid Spanish planta covering both living organism and factory.

shadows.gloss_text: a living organism such as a flower, tree, or grass
a factory or industrial facility

cases.sentence: Children play soccer in the park.
The team will play on Saturday.
The play opened at the small theater.
There is too much play in the steering wheel.
The headline used a play on words.

play.gloss_text: to take part in a game, sport, or playful activity
play.review_notes: Outcome-informed sentinel with game, theater, music, mechanical movement, and phrase uses.

shadows.gloss_text: a dramatic work performed in a theater
looseness or movement in a mechanism

cases.sentence: The state will prosecute the fraud case.
They refused to prosecute without evidence.
Prosecute was printed on the folder tab.

prosecute.gloss_text: to bring legal proceedings against someone

cases.sentence: The choice was purely practical.
The story is purely fictional.
The term purely-functional appeared in the README.

purely.review_notes: Low-polysemy adverb control with hyphenated term no-winner.

cases.sentence: The report summarized the audit findings.
She filed a report after the accident.
New employees report to the office at nine.
The report of the gun echoed through the valley.
The team will report back after lunch.

report.gloss_text: a written or spoken account that gives information
report.review_notes: Outcome-informed sentinel; noun target competes with verb and sound senses.

shadows.gloss_text: to give information officially or formally
a loud explosive sound

cases.sentence: The senate passed the budget bill.
He testified before the senate committee.
The URL senate.gov appeared in the notes.

senate.gloss_text: a legislative body or upper chamber
senate.review_notes: Low-polysemy institutional noun; proper-name mentions are the main negative shape.

cases.sentence: The room was suitable for a workshop.
Choose a suitable password for the account.
The file named suitable.txt was missing.

suitable.gloss_text: appropriate or fitting for a purpose

cases.sentence: The road was closed; therefore, we walked.
The sample was contaminated and therefore unusable.
The proof ended with the word therefore.

therefore.review_notes: Low-polysemy connective; no honest alternate sense is forced.

cases.sentence: The trade between the countries doubled.
Officials debated the new trade agreement.
The children trade cards after school.
He learned a trade from his uncle.
The trade-off was clear after the test.

trade.gloss_text: buying and selling goods or services
trade.review_notes: Commerce target competes with swap and occupation senses.

shadows.gloss_text: to give one thing and receive another
a skilled job or occupation

cases.sentence: The extra step was unnecessary.
They removed unnecessary files from the folder.
The label read unnecessary in red ink.
Install the upgrade before restarting the laptop.
The phone upgrade fixed the battery issue.
The airline offered a free seat upgrade.
The city will upgrade the old bridge next year.
The upgrade path changed after the merger.

upgrade.gloss_text: an update that improves software, hardware, or a system
upgrade.review_notes: Tail word but sense split between technical update and service/status improvement.

shadows.gloss_text: an improved class, room, seat, or level of service
to improve something to a better grade or standard

cases.sentence: She left work early to catch the train.
The repair work took all afternoon.
The old engine will not work in cold weather.
The museum displayed a late work by the painter.
The plan will work out if everyone stays calm.

work.gloss_text: employment, labor, or effort performed by a person
work.review_notes: Noun/verb split plus artwork and mechanism senses make this a good core overload case.

shadows.gloss_text: to operate correctly or have the intended effect
a product of artistic or intellectual effort

cases.sentence: She whispered yes before signing the form.
The answer was yes on the final survey.
The button label reads yes in lowercase letters.

yes.review_notes: Low-polysemy control; no honest alternate English sense is forced.

cases.sentence: The crop yield improved after the rain.
The bond yield fell again today.
Drivers must yield to pedestrians here.
The experiment may yield useful evidence.
She refused to yield to temptation.

yield.gloss_text: the amount produced or the return on an investment
yield.review_notes: Tail rank but strong verb/noun split, good test of advanced-word ambiguity.

shadows.gloss_text: to give way, surrender, or allow another to proceed
to produce or generate a result
